text:
Maya Patel: FYI - AlphaEdge (enterprise analytics) asked for a 6mo POC: private deploy + dedicated pool. They're pushing for 30% off list and full onboarding waived. Also want a data residency clause for eu-west1. Can we greenlight anything without exec?

Tom Rivers: 30% sounds high for 6 months. What's the expected usage? Quick napkin calc: 
```
Projected tokens/mo: 800M
List price est: $24k/mo
6mo list: $144k
30% discount: -$43.2k
Net rev: $100.8k
```
That doesn't account for dedicated infra cost or setup. Finance usually caps pilot discounts at ~20% without a conversion commitment.

Nora Chen: Ops note - we can reduce infra footprint with aggressive KV/prefix caching and burst-only GPUs. For eu-west1 private, a 1-2 node pool (A40 equiv) plus autoscale should be fine. Onboarding labor is ~40 hours -> ~$12k cost.

Maya Patel: They also said procurement timeline is tight: they can prepay up to $150k if we accept 25% and waive onboarding. Prefer upfront wire.

Kai Brooks (deal-desk): We shouldn't accept 30% on a 6mo. Options that usually fly without Exec: 1) 15% + $10k onboarding credit, 2) 20% + 12mo convertible clause (if they convert to annual within X months we keep 20%), 3) 22% if they prepay >= $150k and agree to a short conversion window. Need Legal & Sec signoff for the residency/IP language.

LegalBot: Legal flags: custom residency + data-handling clause needs explicit retention period and export controls. Customer wants "no model retention of prompts" language; we need to translate to: we do not store customer prompt text beyond retention window, but we retain model weights and telemetry. Also need indemnities aligned.

sec-bot: Security checklist: SOC2 cert status (present), penetration test report (pending), KMS integration plan (pending), VPC peering diagram (required), data retention SLA (requested 60-120 days). Current: SOC2 uploaded, pentest scheduled, KMS design doc due by EOD tomorrow.

Tom Rivers: With $150k prepaid, 22% seems reasonable if Legal okays the clause and SecOps signs off on retention. Net math: $150k - $10k onboarding credit (if any) = $140k; that's better margin.

Maya Patel: AlphaEdge prefers waived onboarding, but may accept a $10k credit if it gets the deal over the line. They want the private env ready within 2 weeks of wire.

Nora Chen: Ops can do a soft-provision (non-prod) for smoke tests before wire, but no customer keys until KMS is in place. Provision time for full private cluster ~10 business days once we have go-ahead and billing.

Kai Brooks (deal-desk): I'll propose a counter: 22% off list with a $10k onboarding credit, conditioned on $150k prepaid and a 9-month conversion option (if they sign annual before month 9 we keep 22%). If they refuse onboarding credit, escalate to Sarah.

Maya Patel: Customer responded: they'd prepay $150k for 25% + waived onboarding. They like the 9-month conversion window.

Tom Rivers: Hmm. 25% + waived onboarding is slightly worse than 22% + $10k credit from a cash/margin perspective depending on how we structure accounting. Also waived onboarding reduces our ability to recover labor costs.

LegalBot: If we waive onboarding fee, require explicit SOW language that defines deliverables and limits scope. For residency/IP: propose: "Provider will not persist raw customer prompts beyond 90 days; aggregated telemetry retained per standard policy; provider retains model artifacts."

sec-bot: SecOps notes: retention 90 days is acceptable if customer isolates PII and signs data processing appendix. KMS plan must be implemented before keys are used.

Kai Brooks (deal-desk): Final recommendation from deal-desk: Accept 22% + $10k onboarding credit with $150k prepay AND 9-month conversion. Rationale: preserves margin, gets cash, and keeps onboarding cost partially covered. I'll need written confirmation of the $150k wire + signed DPA (retention clause) and SecOps sign-off to mark as approved.

Maya Patel: I'll ask procurement for wire confirmation and send the SOW with the onboarding credit line: "$10,000 onboarding credit applied to final invoice upon provision." Also I'll ask Legal to push the 90-day retention DPA.

Nora Chen: We'll queue the soft-provision once procurement confirms wire. Ops will prepare VPC diagram and KV warmup plan. No customer keys until KMS doc is signed.

Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. Holding on exec escalation for now. Will update once we have the wire + signed DPA + SecOps sign-off. :thumbsup:

Kai Brooks (deal-desk): Sounds good. If anything slips, I'll escalate to the Head of RevOps. Otherwise I will route final approval to Finance after the docs are attached.

(End of thread)
